captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a modular connector pipe designed with a male joint on one end. The main body is a hollow, smooth cylinder with a consistent outer and inner diameter. At the top, a thinner-walled extension acts as the male insert, featuring four vertical relief cuts (slits) spaced equally around its circumference to allow for slight flexing during press-fit assembly.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric OpenSCAD script for a modular pipe connector with a male joint. The design should allow the user to customize the outer and inner diameters, total pipe length, joint length, joint gap (clearance), and cutout width of the relief slits, using high-resolution cylinders.
captions.factory: The design starts by creating the main hollow pipe body using a difference of two concentric cylinders. On top of this body, a second hollow cylinder with a reduced outer radius (calculated based on outerDiameter, innerDiameter, and jointGap) is added to form the male joint. Finally, four vertical slits are cut out of the joint end by subtracting two perpendicular, thin cubes translated to the top of the pipe.
